post.description:
Stream an agent's response to a user input, including intermediate messages and tokens.

If agent_id is not provided, the default agent will be used.
Use thread_id to persist and continue a multi-turn conversation.
Set ``stream_tokens=false`` to return intermediate messages but not token-by-token.

get.description:
Render a revision to another format of the same kind, without saving
it. ``format`` is a ``Literal`` of every known format so FastAPI/OpenAPI
enumerates and rejects unknown values with a plain 422 before the route
body runs. Unsupported *cross-kind* formats (e.g. exporting a spreadsheet
revision as ``pdf``) still raise ``UnsupportedFormatChangeError`` from the
service (422 via the global handler), so both paths land on 422 but only
the service's own error carries the code/message/details envelope shared
with every other domain rejection in this router.

FlowPlaygroundInlineRunRequest.description:
Playground run for a flow that has never been saved — e.g. still on
the "create agent" form, before an agent_definitions row exists. The
graph travels in the request body instead of being looked up by id,
mirroring Langflow's own build endpoint (vendor/langflow/utils/buildUtils.ts),
which posts the canvas's in-memory nodes/edges directly rather than
requiring a persisted Flow row first.

FlowSpec.title: FlowSpec
FlowSpec.description:
A saved flow: nodes, edges, and canvas viewport.

Node ids are unique and every edge resolves to a known node. Both are
enforced here rather than downstream, because the validator, the compiler
and the canvas all assume it.

Handle.title: Handle
Handle.description:
A named port on a component, accepting or emitting a set of port types.

``expands_from`` turns one declared port into a family: the canvas and the
validator replace it with one handle per row of that field, named by the
row's ``expands_label_key`` column. ``show_when`` makes an output handle
conditional on a sibling field (e.g. Smart Router's ``else`` port only
exists when ``enable_else_output`` is on). Declaring both here keeps them
out of per-component special cases on both sides of the wire.

Auth-only body for binding credentials to an already-registered provider.

Deliberately has no ``name``/``server_url`` fields: an enterprise admin
authenticates a provider a system admin registered, and keeping the url out
of this surface preserves the SSRF boundary the provider/credential split
exists to draw. ``transport`` is accepted because it is auth-adjacent
metadata the auth modal already sends.

is_regenerate.title: Is Regenerate
is_regenerate.description: Set when this send is retrying/regenerating a previous response. The resulting duplicate HumanMessage is stamped so chat history reconstruction can treat the new response as a sibling of the original instead of a new turn.

retry_target_message_id.title: Retry Target Message Id
retry_target_message_id.description: The user message id being retried. When set alongside is_regenerate, the agent invocation forks the LangGraph checkpoint from right after this message instead of appending to the thread's tip, so the new response is generated without the previous (rejected) response in its context.

is_edit.title: Is Edit
is_edit.description: Set when this send is editing the text of a previously-sent user message. Like a retry, the agent invocation forks the LangGraph checkpoint at that message instead of appending to the thread's tip, but the forked message's content is replaced with the edited text before generating a new response — so everything after the edited message (its old response and any later turns) is excluded from the new response's context, while remaining permanently reachable via the old branch.

edit_target_message_id.title: Edit Target Message Id
edit_target_message_id.description: The user message id being edited. Required when is_edit is set. Unlike retry_target_message_id (which points at the message being retried, i.e. the same message the new response attaches to), this points at the message whose own content is being replaced.

edit_target_message_id.description: The user message id being edited. Required when is_edit is set. Unlike retry_target_message_id (which points at the message being retried, i.e. the same message the new response attaches to), this points at the message whose own content is being replaced.

document_context.description: The document currently open in the client's side panel, if any. Exposed to document tools as run context (`configurable["active_document"]`); never injected into the conversation history.
